item.description:

As the adventurers investigate the source of this peculiar curse, they must contend with the looming threat of being transformed into turkeys themselves while racing to uncover the truth behind the magical mishap. item.title: Tired of Doing All The Heavy Lifting in Your Relationships? — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM — The Space
item.description: Are you the one who always remembers, plans, initiates conversations, keeps the peace, and makes sure everyone else is okay? Whether it’s your marriage, partnership, family, friendships, or other relationships, carrying the emotional weight can leave you feeling exhausted, overwhelmed, and disconnected. Join Sakirat Oladiran, Nurse Practitioner and Certified Life & Health Coach, for an intimate and supportive wellness gathering designed for women. We’ll explore how relationship stress impacts your physical and emotional health, why you may find yourself carrying more than your share, and practical ways to communicate your needs, establish healthy boundaries, and create more balanced, fulfilling connections. This is an opportunity to pause, reflect, feel heard, and walk away with practical strategies to support both your relationships and your well-being. Come as you are. Leave with a fresh perspective and tools to create healthier connections. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens

item.title: Three Stories. One Screen. | The Official Film Showcase — Sat Nov 21, 1:30 PM — The Clairidge
item.description: Dive into three stories on one screen at The Official Film Showcase—live and in person at The Clairidge in Montclair, NJ! Headlining the afternoon is End of the Line: Brotherhood, a raw, poignant feature drama examining end-of-life dignity, caregiver burnout, and the historical roots of healthcare distrust in the Black community through the lens of an underfunded inner-city hospice clinic. Shot using 6K digital cinema technology, the film features an ensemble cast including veteran actors Christopher Mann (The Wire, Creed III) and Nakia Dillard (The Wire, Black Lightning). The program also showcases the exclusive premiere of short drama Wedding Night and psychological thriller Lady in the Mirror. Guests will enjoy light food, networking opportunities, and an interactive post-screening filmmaker talkback with cast and crew from all films discussing the story, production journey, and social impact behind the work. Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Time: 1:30 PM – 5:00 PM EST Venue: The

item.title: 🍂🥾 Back on the trails w/Ivette! 5+miles 🌲🥾 — Sun Nov 22, 10:00 AM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group ***There’s no better way to make a comeback than with good company and a great trail! After being sidelined for a while, I am thrilled to finally lace-up-and-go and I’d love for you to join me for a scenic stroll through the woods from Greenwood Gardens to Hemlock Falls via the Rahway River! It’s going to be a great way to get outside, catch up, and enjoy the crisp air.*** ***I can't wait to see everyone out there!***
**A few quick tips before we head out:** **- Dress warm: Wear weather-appropriate layers so you stay comfortable.** **- Gear: Hiking poles are recommended, especially for the river crossing.**
***📢*** ***- This event is specifically geared towards 50+ community*** ***- No pets please***
**What to bring for a Hike: Water, Hiking Shoes/Boots - No sneakers, Snacks, Trekking Poles and Spikes (optional), and a Talking Point! Dress for the weather and in Light Layers.** **Steady rain or snow cancels the hike.**

Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.

item.description:

Having chaired the Building and Grounds (B&G) Committee for many years, Ken wanted to recreate the fellowship that would happen on B&G Work Day events when parishioners volunteered time to clean up and repair items around the Church's campus. Ken scheduled a Saturday morning once a month at the Pilgrim Diner in Cedar Grove with a group of 6-8 guys during which they would share conversation and life experience with one another. This breakfast group will now meet on the second Saturday of each month from 8:30 to 10am (unless otherwise indicated on the website calendar). For more information, speak with Father Jerry or Ken Traficante.

Montclair Robotics is a 100% student-led high school robotics team that participates in FIRST Robotics Competition. The team has over 80 student members who spend months designing, building, programming, and promoting a 125-pound robot. The team prides itself on creating an inclusive environment where there are no tryouts or prior required skills. No student is turned away if they are unable to pay their dues. In addition to learning engineering skills, gain leadership experience, build confidence, and participate in community outreach events. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Nov 25, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

item.description:
This is a free Adult School class.
Rod Serling wrote a few stories for The Twilight Zone about the holiday spirit and specifically, about Christmas. Born on December 25th in 1924, Rod was known to often say, ”I came as a present unwrapped.” Though Rod was Jewish, he and his family enjoyed celebrating Christmas among friends and neighbors in his hometown of Binghamton, NY.
Two of his wonderfully creative holiday episodes will be presented and discussed in the upcoming micro-marathon.
The first is entitled, “The Night of the Meek”: S2:E11 A downtrodden, drunken department store Santa angers his employers and is fired from his job. He wanders aimlessly in the streets of the city until he finds a magic sack that is filled with gifts that can fulfill everyone’s wish, including his. Art Carney is stellar as the Santa Claus that finds his “True North”.

item.title: Amedeo Modigliani: Bohemian of Montmartre and Montparnasse — Wed Dec 2, 1:30 PM — Montclair Public Library
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. You can register here.
Amedeo Modigliani, painter and sculptor, was born in Italy to a middle class, cultured Jewish family. He spent most of his tragically short life in France among the avant-garde artists of bohemian Paris. He is known for portraits and nudes in a contemporary style characterized by the elongation of faces and figures. Come and hear about this quintessentially unconventional artist and see many of his ravishing paintings and expressive sculptures. Some of his works are featured in the outstanding upcoming exhibition at the Brooklyn Museum, From Cezanne to Modigliani.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306
